title: Best Browser Privacy Tools Compared
metaDescription: How Brave, Firefox, Safari, Chrome and Incognito Browser (which we make) compare on privacy defaults, blocking, fingerprinting, transparency and HTTPS.
intro: Choosing the right privacy browser is one of the simplest ways to protect your personal data online, because major browsers collect user information by default. This page compares five browsers on the same five criteria, and each rating is worked out from the table.

products.name: Brave Browser
products.tagline: Privacy by default with built-in ad blocking
pros: Blocks ads and trackers by default
cons: Some websites may break with strict blocking

products.name: Mozilla Firefox
products.tagline: Open-source browser with enhanced tracking protection
pros: Enhanced Tracking Protection on by default
cons: Strict tracking protection can break some sites

products.name: Incognito Browser
products.tagline: Android browser that stays in private mode and wipes history, cookies and sessions when you exit
pros: Every tab is private; history, cookies and sessions are wiped when you exit
Keeps no browsing history or cache on the device (downloads are kept)
Built-in ad blocker with a High Security Blocking option
Settings to switch images, JavaScript and cookies on or off
cons: Android only: there is no iOS, desktop or web version
No fingerprinting protection, tracker blocking or HTTPS-only mode is documented
Google Play's Data safety section says it may collect crash logs and diagnostics

products.name: Apple Safari
products.tagline: Apple's browser for Mac, iPhone and iPad

products.name: Google Chrome
products.tagline: Popular browser with optional privacy features
cons: Google's business model relies on data

features.name: Default Privacy Settings
features.description: How well the browser protects privacy without manual configuration

brave-browser.note: Blocks ads and trackers by default

incognito-browser.note: Private mode is always on; history, cookies and sessions are wiped on exit

features.name: Ad & Tracker Blocking
features.description: Built-in ability to block advertisements and tracking scripts

incognito-browser.note: Built-in ad blocker with a High Security Blocking option; tracker blocking is not documented

features.name: Fingerprinting Protection
features.description: Prevention of device fingerprinting techniques used for tracking

mozilla-firefox.note: Blocks known fingerprinting scripts by default; Mozilla's stronger protections are on only in private windows and Strict mode

incognito-browser.note: Not claimed. Agent Cloaking changes the browser and device a site sees, which is not fingerprint protection

apple-safari.note: Limits known fingerprinting scripts in all browsing; its strongest tracking-and-fingerprinting setting is on by default only in Private Browsing

features.name: Data Collection Transparency
features.description: Clear disclosure of what data is collected and how it's used

brave-browser.note: Publishes a detailed privacy policy; its product analytics can be turned off

incognito-browser.note: Google Play's Data safety section: may collect app info, crash logs and diagnostics; none shared with third parties

features.name: Secure Connection Features
features.description: HTTPS enforcement and secure connection capabilities

brave-browser.note: Upgrades connections to HTTPS by default

incognito-browser.note: No HTTPS-only or HTTPS-upgrade mode is documented

verdict.summary: On these five criteria Brave scores highest, followed by Firefox, Safari, Chrome and Incognito Browser. Brave blocks ads and trackers and randomizes fingerprinting data without any setup. Firefox comes next and is open source, though some of its protections need configuring. Safari's tracking protection is on by default, but its strongest tracking-and-fingerprinting setting is on by default only in Private Browsing, and it runs only on Apple devices. Chrome needs settings changes and extensions to catch up. Incognito Browser, which we make, keeps every tab private and wipes history, cookies and sessions when you exit, but it documents no fingerprinting protection, tracker blocking or HTTPS-only mode, so it scores lowest here.

bestFor.reason: Blocks ads and trackers by default with no configuration needed
Open-source with extensive customization and privacy extensions
Built into macOS, iOS and iPadOS, with tracking protection on by default

pro_tips: Always use private/incognito mode for sensitive browsing, but remember it doesn't hide activity from your ISP or websites
Install privacy-focused extensions like uBlock Origin and Privacy Badger on browsers that don't have built-in blocking
Regularly clear cookies and browsing data, or set your browser to do this automatically when closing
Disable location tracking, camera, and microphone permissions for websites that don't need them
Consider using a VPN alongside your privacy browser for additional protection, especially on public Wi-Fi networks

faqs.question: Which browser is most secure for online banking?
faqs.answer: This page doesn't score banking security. Any up-to-date mainstream browser, such as Brave, Firefox, Safari or Chrome, is fine for banking if you keep it updated, avoid extensions you don't need, and check that you're on your bank's real website. On this page's privacy criteria, Brave scores highest, followed by Firefox.

faqs.question: Does private browsing mode completely hide my activity?
faqs.answer: No. Private browsing stops your browser keeping history on your device, but your internet provider, your employer's or school's network, and the websites you visit can still see your activity. A VPN hides the sites you visit from your network, and a browser that blocks trackers limits what websites learn; neither makes you anonymous.

faqs.question: Can I make Chrome as private as other browsers?
faqs.answer: You can make Chrome more private with its settings, such as blocking third-party cookies and turning on 'Always use secure connections', and with blocking extensions. Its defaults still collect more data than Brave or Firefox, though, and its fingerprinting protection is limited.

faqs.question: Are privacy browsers slower than regular browsers?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Blocking ads and trackers leaves a page fewer scripts to load, but how fast a browser feels depends on your device and the sites you use. This page doesn't score speed, because we have no independent measurements to cite.

faqs.question: What's the difference between incognito mode and a privacy browser?
faqs.answer: Incognito mode, Chrome's name for a private window, only stops your browser keeping history, cookies and form data after you close the window. Browsers such as Brave also block trackers and ads while you browse, and some add fingerprinting defences. Neither hides your activity from your internet provider.
